plain_what: Instead of comparing the current word with every earlier word, the model sends a query down a small tree of geometric addresses and picks up the single earlier word sitting at the end of that path. It makes one hard choice per step by walking a tree, and never scores the whole history.
how_it_works: Per 8-dimensional block b of the model width, the query is the integer vector at the last position. At each tree level the query is acted on by a learned signed-axis permutation (one of 64 group elements; coordinates are permuted and sign-flipped by table lookup). At level 0 the nearest of up to 16 frontier roots is chosen; at later levels the nearest of 3 children. Nearest means the smallest (L1 distance, coordinate Hamming, port id) to one of the 16 roots of a single E8 orbit. Each choice composes a precomputed BFS transport action between roots, so total = BFS[root -> goal] composed with total. The ternary BinderPlan tree built over the context ends in leaves that are earlier positions; the output is the accumulated action applied to the chosen leaf's carrier vector. Cost is levels x 16 comparisons, independent of how many earlier positions exist (context cap 243). Port selection never inspects which token a leaf holds, so content enters only through the query's geometry. Learning is discrete: each route parameter is tried against its 15 generator moves in a counterfactual forward pass, the best strictly improving move is applied, and nothing is differentiated. The output vector goes to the shared writer (see admission).
geometry: One 16-root E8 orbit as the routing atlas; signed-axis action group of order 64; BFS transport tables between roots; SpiralCore ternary BinderPlan tree. Float-era forms used prime/UOR addresses, H4/binary-icosahedral (2I) roots, Hopf sectors, Lorentz scores and a spanning tree over cells.

status_reason: ReadSpec::Route is the base read of every trained discrete artifact: rung-0 seed 1 (149 top-1 of 14,287) and the four K16 runs (docs/labs/k16-outcome-call-2026-10-19/README.md). But no read-off/read-on ablation exists and Route got only 20 proposals in 16,404 updates, so its contribution is unattributed (docs/labs/attention-state-2026-10-18/README.md).
reopen_conditions: Float-era variants (spanning-tree router with tangent and normal nulls, read_lineage as addressing rather than scoring) are open but unregistered; they may be re-registered as an offline float sheet under D37 with a fresh FIT, a D11 integer export and a reported export gap.
A fair Route test needs a codebook whose addresses are distinct (injective or address-structured cells) so that a read can be judged at all.
A fair Route test needs a read-off/read-on ablation with enough read proposals in the schedule (an interleaved schedule or a dedicated Route stage).

rule_compat.D11: Kernel uses table gather, sign flip, compare and integer add only (discrete.cu header comment); no float, no multiply in model values. The audited records contain no D11 served export or export-gap measurement for a trained discrete Route artifact.
rule_compat.D23: Compliant: hard argmin by (L1, Hamming, port); no softmax, sigmoid, tanh or exponential anywhere in forward, objective or credit. The float-era Lorentz and M1 router configurations used a softmax read and were cancelled for it.
rule_compat.D30: Compliant: no matmul or GEMM; the 8x8 'rotation' is a signed axis permutation read from a table.
rule_compat.D32_D37: D32 integer, GPU-only, counterfactual move learning; training of the discrete path stays held except under separately released, owner-typed scoped runs (D40). D37 would allow a float-trained Route only as a new FIT'd pre-registration with a D11 export.

never_tested: Route versus no read (read-off ablation) and Route versus Flock on a codebook with distinct addresses.
Route trained with a schedule that gives it more than 20 proposals in 16,404 updates.
The tangent-null and normal-null controls (move the address along the manifold vs across a branch) that the invariant-addressed-read brief requires to show the geometry is load-bearing.
Spanning-tree addressing as addressing: read_lineage variants were only ever measured as scoring changes.
Served tokens per second and cost of a routed read against a scored read at long context.
Content-aware port selection (ports are chosen by the query's geometry, never by what the leaves hold).
failed_only_on_configuration: Prime-route attention (#958) and trajectory routing (docs/trajectory_routing_946.md): closed as storage/recall-only or inert in a product probe; they say nothing about routing inside a trained integer read.

read_lineage scorer configurations and the M1 router campaign were cancelled at 2/3 seeds under D23/D24 for a softmax/host fallback; a configuration, not a mechanism negative (docs/mechanisms/README.md status table).
Integrated attention A1-A4 (Sept 24): authored 24-example panels, soft or float selectors; failures traced to write gates and selector retention, not to routing by address.
Rung-0 seed 1 and the K16 runs: judged on a codebook with 16 distinct vectors where only 16 address classes exist, so the read could not be separated from codebook drift.
Lorentz vs l2: a scoring comparison inside a softmax read, inactive under D23.
open_questions: How much of the 149 top-1 does the learned Route contribute, if any?
Can a Route that never looks at leaf content reach the copy-successor targets (3,847 of 14,287) that the finite-relational-head brief says Route and Flock provably cannot express?
Which invariant should be the address: a prime/UOR address, an icosian phase, or a composition?
Is a single 16-root orbit enough atlas, or does the read need the full orbit (lib.rs notes this is not full-orbit learnability)?
related: flock-read: same kernel family; replaces Route's single leaf with a transported consensus of K kept neighbours
relation-read: adds an exact-relation reranker on top of Flock, targeting what Route cannot express
admission: the writer that consumes the routed vector; admission, not routing, is the measured ceiling
address-cells: the codebook that gives positions their addresses
prime-zeta-codebook: the injective initialiser that makes addresses distinct
exact-memory: the older idea of routing a query to an exact prime address
spiralcore-fbs: supplies the BFS transport and ternary tree
discrete-learning: the counterfactual choose/apply law that trains the route parameters
figure_ideas: A ternary tree drawn over a row of context tokens (leaves). The query enters at the top; at each level three child ports are lit with their L1 distances to the 16 roots, the nearest is highlighted, and a rotation arrow accumulates down the path until one leaf is picked.

The 16 roots of the orbit drawn as 16 points on a ring, with the query vector as a moving point. As a route action changes (a learning move), the query rotates and the chosen port jumps from one root to another.
Side-by-side cost bars: comparisons per step for a scored read (grows with context) against the routed read (flat at levels x 16), at contexts 192, 1,536 and 4,096.
